question: How do vijñānākala and pralayākala arise from the same knower?
premises: The balanced supreme-and-non-supreme knower is declared vijñānākala.
That vijñānākala has an awakened supreme aspect.
Through predominance of the lower aspect, that same knower is pralayākala.
inference: Vijñānākala and pralayākala are two states of the same knower distinguished by the relative predominance of supreme and lower aspects.
plain_english: He is declared the vijñānākala, with the supreme aspect awakened; through the predominance of the lower aspect, that same one is the pralayākala.
